# Strategy A notes: Momentum

## Entry rules
- Buy names with positive 20-day AND 60-day returns that trade above their 50-day average.
- Rank by 60d trend first, then 20d. No holding is "core". Every position follows the same rules.
- Skip any name with a single-day spike of more than 5%.
- A name more than 15% above its 50d average is extended. Skip it.
- Hold at most 1 name from the high-beta tech/semis cluster (AMD, META and PLTR caused the biggest losses).
- Prefer sector ETFs (XLV, XLI, XLF, XLP, XLE) or large low-beta leaders (V, MA, KO). Spreads are tighter.
- Don't buy a name that overlaps a current holding (e.g. XLP while holding KO).

## Sizing
- Hold 3-4 positions, keeping $15-25 in cash. Right now about $65 is idle. Deploy about $45 into one qualifying name from a sector we don't hold (industrials or financials preferred). If nothing qualifies, hold the cash rather than force a trade.
- Use confidence 4-5. Never go above 5. Tournament data: 1-4 averaged -1.47% (n=6), 5-7 averaged -5.49% (n=12), 8-10 averaged -8.61% (n=2). Higher confidence keeps doing worse.

## Exits and rotation
- Hard stop: sell at 8% below entry. The XLE stop filled at -9.2% because the check came a day late. Write the stop price for each holding below and check it every day.
- Early warning: sell at -6% or worse if the name is also below its 50d average, has a negative 20d return, or has dropped out of the 20d leaders. Once a holding drops out of the 20d leaders, treat -5% as the trigger. XLE dropped out and kept sliding.
- Rotate out when a holding closes below its 50d average, or when its 20d return turns negative and it drops out of the top names.
- Hold at least 3 trading days unless a stop triggers.
- Spread penalties are now $4.16, about 0.8% of capital. Make at most one trade per day. Only rotate into a clearly higher-ranked name.
- Don't take profits just because a position is up.

## Levels (entry / -6% / -8% stop)
- XLV: 184.48 / 173.41 / 169.72
- KO: 96.00 / 90.24 / 88.32
- V: take the entry price from the position record and compute both levels on the first day.

## Status
- Week: -2.28% vs SPY -2.64% (beat SPY). Since start: -11.99% vs SPY -5.08%.
- Holding V, XLV and KO, a defensive mix that suits a falling market. Let the rules run and don't chase a rebound in extended tech.

# Strategy B notes: Mean reversion

## Status
- Since start: -0.05% vs SPY -5.08%. Mostly cash; the only position is XOM (~$76, about 15% of the account).
- Open trade: XOM 0.4501 filled @169.43. Stop 158 (-6.7%), take profit 175 (+3.3%), time stop 11/20. Check all three at the start of every decision. Because the fill came in about 1.7% above the limit, the exit levels are now lopsided. If XOM closes below ~161 (-5% from the fill), exit.

## Entry setup (core)
- Look for liquid names with a sharp 5-day drop of about 2x their normal 5-day move or more, with the 60-day trend intact and price near or above its 50d MA.
- Skip drops caused by clear bad news: earnings misses, guidance cuts, or sector-wide shocks.
- During a broad selloff, wait for a stabilization day (SPY up, or the 5-day drop stops getting worse). Then make one small entry per day at most.

## Deploying cash
- Cash protected the lead, but it can't beat SPY in a rebound. On each new stabilization day, add one more intact-trend dip from a different sector than the current holdings (financials, healthcare, staples, industrials). Target 2-4 positions and 40-60% of the account invested, built up over several days.
- If SPY makes a new -3% or worse day, pause new buys. Keep the existing positions unless their stops are hit.

## Costs and orders
- Spread penalties are now $5.29 (~1.06% of the account). Trade only large, tight-spread names, with each position ≥ ~$70.
- Fills come in 1-3% worse than the limit. Set the limit at or slightly below the last price. **Recompute the stop and take profit from the actual fill price.** Skip a trade if the bounce left from a realistic fill is under ~3%.

## Exits (mechanical)
- Write down the stop, take profit and time stop at entry and re-base them on the fill.
- On the time-stop date, sell that day (NVDA lesson: holding past it cost about $3).
- Exit if price closes at or below the stop, or is within ~1% of it on a down-market day. Exit right away on bad news.
- Defaults: take profit about +5% from the fill, cut at -5%, time stop about 10 trading days.

## Confidence
- Tournament data: conf 1-4 averaged -1.47% (6 buys), 5-7 averaged -5.49% (12), 8-10 averaged -8.61% (2). Higher confidence keeps doing worse.
- Default buys to conf 3. Use 4-5 only for a textbook setup after stabilization with a clean news check. Never go above 5.
notes.C:
# Strategy C notes: Catalyst reader

## Identity
Trade only when a specific headline explains a price move, or explains why a stock didn't move. Look for over- and under-reactions. Holding cash is allowed. Most of the lead over SPY (−0.90% vs SPY −5.08% since start) comes from holding cash in falling weeks. That isn't catalyst skill, and it will lag in a rising week.

## Entry rules
- Each session, name the best catalyst setup and give it a verdict: (a) what the news changes over 12 months, (b) whether the move is bigger than that, (c) buy, or hold with a specific reason.
- **Watchlist carry-forward:** check every flagged-but-skipped overreaction first, every session. This worked in W5 (GOOGL was revisited and bought). Drop a name after 5 sessions or if the thesis breaks.
- **Overreaction (>5% on specific news):** buy only after a green close that also **beats SPY by at least 1% that day**, or a full session holding above the prior low. A green day that comes from a broad rally isn't stock-specific confirmation (W5 GOOGL was bought on a midterm rally day, then fell with the sector).
- **No headline, no trade.** Skip big moves that no news explains.
- **Underreaction:** concrete material news with less than a 1% move. Log one named candidate **every session**. It was skipped on most W5 days, and it's the only way to make money in up weeks.
- Prefer single-company catalysts. Stay out while a sector or macro selloff keeps adding bad news. Don't buy into structural downtrends or real fundamental damage.

## Data hygiene
- If every price shows 0.0%, the data is stale: hold, and say so.

## Sizing and confidence
- Tournament results: confidence 1–4 avg −1.47% (n=6), 5–7 −5.49% (n=12), 8–10 −8.61% (n=2). Higher confidence has done worse every week so far.
- Starters use confidence 3–4. Never go above 6. Add only after a further confirmed close that beats SPY. Hold at most 2 positions.

## Exits
- **Time stop, applied strictly:** session 1 is the fill day. If the position is below cost at the end of session 3, exit at the next decision. Don't grant extensions; in W5 the trader gave GOOGL "one more session".
- **Thesis break:** if new negative news widens the story, exit or cut by half.
- **Take profit** once about half the overreaction has retraced.

## Log

- W2: −0.83% vs SPY −1.96%. Bought SMH too early.
- W3: +0.30% vs SPY −0.42%. SMH time-stop exit −2.8%.
- W4: −0.02% vs SPY −0.54%. 0 trades, and flagged names were never followed up.
- W5: −0.33% vs SPY −2.64%. GOOGL starter (conf 4) @291.07 bought on a broad-rally green day, now about −2%. Due for a time-stop exit if still below cost.

# Strategy D notes: Small-cap explorer

Identity: find tradable small-cap opportunities that SPY doesn't capture. Record: 1 trade in 6 weeks (KD, Tier 3 starter). We're at -0.76% since start and SPY is at -5.08%. Most of that gap comes from sitting in cash. It is not edge yet.

## Open position: KD (2.8571 sh, entry 17.49)
- Stop: sell on a close below 15.2. Target: about 22, which is 2x risk.
- Time stop: if neither stop nor target has hit, sell at the 11/10 close (3 sessions after the fill). Don't extend the hold or add to it.

## What the data looks like
- The mover list shows extremes: ±25% or more, warrants, illiquid names, and leveraged ETFs. The 3–15% band has been empty for 4 weeks. If it's empty, say so in one line.
- The day's range is often not shown.

## Screening
- Drop warrants, units, rights, leveraged or inverse ETFs, anything under $0.50, volume under $1M, spreads over 1.5%, and moves of ±40% or more. Don't comment on them.
- Tier 1: names moving ±3–15% with a spread of 1.5% or less and real volume.
- Tier 2 (watchlist): liquid names moving 15–40%. Buy only on day-2 continuation or a stabilized 30–50% pullback. If the name isn't visible the next day, drop it.
- Tier 3 (day-1 starter, max 1 per week): an up-move of 15–35%, spread ≤0.5%, volume ≥$10M, and a news catalyst. If the day's range can't be seen, the trade is still allowed, but put the limit about 3–5% below the close instead of at it. KD filled at the full price the next day while SPY fell 4% and dropped 7% right away. Confidence 3, smallest size, stop at the midpoint between the prior close and entry, target 2x risk, max hold 3 sessions.
- No new entries on days SPY is down 2% or more.

## Entry and sizing
- Confidence 3–4, max 2 names, limit orders only. Don't chase.
- The expected move must be at least 3x the spread.

## Exits
- Set the stop, target and time stop before buying. Follow them mechanically and don't hold through binary events.

## Confidence
- Tournament-wide: buys at 1–4 averaged -1.47% (n=6), 5–7 averaged -5.49% (n=12), 8–10 averaged -8.61% (n=2). That makes 2 weeks in a row where higher confidence went with worse results.
- Default is 3. Use 5 only with a fresh catalyst, spread ≤1%, and a clean chart. Never use 6 or higher.

# Strategy E: Claude's pick: QQQ/SPY core, lower tilt in drawdowns, very few trades

## Approach
QQQ held against SPY is a beta/tech bet, not a proven edge. Since the start we are -10.8% vs SPY -5.1%. Most of that gap comes from QQQ falling harder in tech-led selloffs plus the earlier META earnings loss. Not trading saves spread but doesn't create alpha by itself. Keep the tilt, but make it smaller while the market is weak.

## Target allocation (rebalance at most once per week, only if more than 7 points off target)
- **SPY below its 50-day average (or can't verify): QQQ about 55%, SPY about 40%, cash 5% or less.** That applies now. Make ONE rebalance trade this week: sell QQQ, buy SPY.
- SPY above its 50-day on 3 consecutive verified closes: go back to QQQ about 70%, SPY about 25%.
- If a rule's data can't be verified, do nothing on that rule. Don't keep re-citing unverifiable rules.

## Single stocks
- Only while SPY is above its 50-day. At most 1 per week, sized 10%, funded from SPY.
- Must be a US large cap (over $10B) with average daily volume over $50M. Price must be above a rising 50-day, and the 50-day above the 200-day. Skip anything up more than 15% in 3 days.
- Never hold one within 5 trading days of earnings. Sell it 2 sessions before the report.
- Exits: a close 8% below entry, or 2 closes more than 2% below the 50-day. Proceeds go to SPY.

## Orders
- Limit price: last to +0.3%. If an order expires twice, drop it. No trades under $25. Sweep cash only once it exceeds 8%.

## Confidence
- Higher confidence has done worse. Tournament-wide: conf 1-4 averaged -1.5%, conf 5-7 -5.5%, conf 8-10 -8.6%. Treat confidence as a log entry only. Always use the minimum size and never size up on conviction.

## Habits
- The default is HOLD apart from the regime rebalance above. 0-1 trades per week. Log a one-line reason for each trade.
